payload:019d027a-152f-76a2-afe0-ec62eee49304|019d48a2-4143-7aa0-b178-e6950b06b347|No, these are **backend-side files**, not something the UI automatically “triggers” just by existing.

What they are:

- [memory-services.ts](/Users/divyansh/Arceus/server/src/services/memory-services.ts)
  - This is just a **service registry/wiring file**.
  - It decides which memory helper services get created.
  - It is not a route by itself.

- [memory-projections.ts](/Users/divyansh/Arceus/server/src/services/memory-projections.ts)
  - This is now a **small backend helper** for memory explorer/promotion-log shaping.
  - Earlier it had graph behavior.
  - I trimmed it so it no longer depends on graph RPC methods, but I kept it because some non-graph memory endpoints still use it.

- [routes/memory.ts](/Users/divyansh/Arceus/server/src/routes/memory.ts)
  - This is the **HTTP route layer** for memory APIs.
  - The UI hits these endpoints when you open memory-related screens.

Will they be triggered when you run the UI?

- **Not just by starting the UI**
  - starting the UI does not automatically execute all memory routes
- **Yes when you open memory screens or actions that call memory APIs**
  - for example:
    - agent memory tab
    - memory summary
    - habits
    - priming
    - memory explorer
    - promotions feed

Important nuance:
- the **graph-specific routes and graph UI were removed**
- the remaining files are still used for **non-graph memory features**

So these files are still “live,” but only for normal memory functionality, not the deleted graph layer.

If you want, I can show you a very simple map:

`UI memory tab -> routes/memory.ts -> memory-services.ts -> memory-projections.ts / other memory services`

and tell you exactly which tab calls which route.
